summary: CaptionIQ v1 milestone tested end-to-end. Backend 12/13 pytest cases pass (auth register/login/me/logout/refresh, Google OAuth session simulation via mongo, projects CRUD + ownership isolation, media upload/stream with HTTP Range 206, REAL Whisper + gpt-5.4 entity tagging, caption save). Frontend full journey (signup -> dashboard -> new-project dialog -> upload speech.mp3 -> studio -> transcribe -> logout -> protected route redirect -> login re-lists project) all pass. Primary AI feature (transcription+entity tagging) verified rendering 12 caption-word elements with 2 person + 2 location + 2 action entities. ONE CRITICAL BUG: brute-force lockout does not fire behind the k8s ingress because request.client.host is the ingress proxy peer IP which varies across requests, splitting the 5-attempt counter across identifiers.

Emergent Google OAuth session flow - pass (simulated per playbook) - evidence: injected users doc + user_sessions doc into mongo test_database, then GET /api/auth/me with Authorization: Bearer <session_token> returned 200 with auth_provider=google and correct email - skill: ai-testing-core

critical.issue: Brute-force lockout does NOT activate at 5 wrong attempts through the preview URL. Root cause: _check_lockout uses identifier = f"{request.client.host}:{email}", but request.client.host is the direct TCP peer (the k8s ingress-proxy IP), which varies request-to-request. Verified in mongo: after 5 wrong logins the login_attempts collection shows only count=4 on one identifier '10.219.1.32:...' and the 6th correct login succeeded with 200 instead of 429. Fix: use X-Forwarded-For (right-most before trusted hops) as the client IP, or key the lockout on email alone (with a wider window) so it can't be split across ingress pods.

minor.issue: Cookies are Secure+SameSite=None. This is required for the studio to work over HTTPS, but any non-HTTPS testing path will silently drop cookies -- rely on Bearer tokens from the response body when curling.

issues: React warning: 'Missing Description or aria-describedby={undefined} for DialogContent' — add DialogDescription for a11y.

action_items: Fix brute-force lockout to work behind k8s ingress: derive the real client IP from X-Forwarded-For (or just rate-limit on email) so 5 wrong logins from the same real client actually flip _check_lockout to 429.
Add DialogDescription (or aria-describedby) to the New Project dialog to remove the a11y warning.
critical_code_review_comments: backend/auth.py lockout identifier is IP+email, but request.client.host behind an ingress is the ingress-proxy IP and can change per request (multi-replica ingress or connection pooling). This breaks the primary anti-brute-force control. Confirmed with a live 5-attempt test: only 4 of 5 counted on one identifier and 6th correct login went through with 200.
backend/projects.py list_projects hardcodes .to_list(1000). Fine for MVP but paginate before scale.
backend/storage.py init_storage stores the session key in a module global — for multi-worker uvicorn each worker will lazy-init separately (fine, just noting).
backend/transcription.py entity tagger silently swallows LLM errors and returns empty tag sets. Users would just see uncolored words. Consider logging at ERROR and surfacing a status somewhere.

context_for_next_testing_agent: pytest suite lives at /app/backend/tests/test_captioniq.py — needs REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL + MONGO_URL + DB_NAME env vars, runs the full stack including a live Whisper+gpt-5.4 call (~8s wall time). test_five_wrong_logins_lockout will keep failing until the ingress-IP problem in auth.py is fixed. Fixture /app/test_fixtures/speech.mp3 is small (37 KB) and reliably transcribes to the same text.
rca of the issue: Brute-force lockout counter is split across multiple identifiers because the app derives the client IP via `request.client.host`, which under k8s ingress equals the ingress-pod peer IP. Since a single external client can be routed to different ingress pods (or the peer IP can change on connection reuse), 5 wrong logins from the same user do not all land on the same identifier row. Mongo evidence: login_attempts had a single row with count=4 and no locked_until set. Reproduction: hit POST /api/auth/login 5 times with a wrong password against the preview URL for the same email — expected 429 on the 5th or 6th call, actual is 401/200. Fix options: (a) read X-Forwarded-For (starlette exposes it in request.headers) and use the first value or the last public IP, (b) drop IP from the identifier and lock the account by email only for a shorter window, or (c) use a proxy-aware middleware like starlette's ProxyHeadersMiddleware / uvicorn --proxy-headers with `--forwarded-allow-ips='*'`.
